https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/2/23.body: Save Share Remote Tajikistan region shaken by magnitude 6.8 earthquake on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Published On 23 Feb 2023 23 Feb 2023 A series of earthquakes has hit a remote region of Tajikistan bordering China, with the strongest temblor measured at magnitude 6.8, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS). The quake struck at about 5:37am (00:37 GMT) on Thursday about 65km (40 miles) west of Murghob near the border with China’s Xinjiang province, USGS and the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) said. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 After surviving earthquake, Syrian family of seven dies in fire list 2 of 3 ‘We’re living but we’re dead’: No peace for survivors in Adiyaman list 3 of 3 Turkey to end earthquake rescue operations end of list Murghob is the district capital with a population of a few thousand in the Pamir Mountains. No casualties were immediately reported. The area is sparsely populated but is home to the Sarez Lake which could potentially flood vast areas in several countries if disrupted. The lake was formed by a 1911 earthquake that caused a landslide that dammed the Murghab River, according to USGS. The area has experienced at least 18 earthquakes of a magnitude 6.5 or larger over the last century. In 2015, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck 105km (65 miles) west of Murghob, killing two and destroying hundreds of homes. During the most recent earthquakes, tremors were felt in capital Dushanbe about 700km (435 miles) to the west. The quake was strongly felt across the border in some areas of Kashgar prefecture and Kizilsu Kyrgyz autonomous prefecture in Xinjiang, but no casualties or damage has been reported so far, state media CCTV said, citing local information officers. The China Earthquake Networks Center said it was a magnitude 7.2 quake, with the epicentre 10km (6 miles) deep. Measurements by different agencies often differ. Advertisement

https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2.body: This press release contains information that some readers may find upsetting Meta failed to address harmful rhetoric on Facebook against the LGBTI community in Hungary by ineffectively applying its own moderation policies, a new Amnesty International briefing shows. ‘It erodes my soul’: Meta’s contribution to anti-LGBTI discourse in Hungary , shows how Meta’s policy decisions, including the weakening of safeguards for high risk groups in January 2025 and the significant reduction in proactive content moderation, have negatively affected the LGBTI community in Hungary. “Meta contributed to adverse human rights impacts experienced by LGBTI people in Hungary through its policy decisions, and failed to take adequate steps to prevent the resulting harm. Risks to LGBTI people in Hungary were foreseeable and well documented, yet Meta did not adequately act on them, Daniela Schnidrig, Interim Policy and Advocacy Adviser at Amnesty International’s Big Tech Accountability Team. One of Meta’s failures was not properly assessing the risks that changes to its global policies posed to the Hungarian LGBTI community. This was despite knowing the hostile political climate and existing legal restrictions on LGBTI-related assemblies, including Pride, and sustained anti-LGBTI rhetoric, including by government and government-aligned actors. Facebook occupies a uniquely influential position within Hungary’s information environment, reaching over half of the population. LGBTI people interviewed for this research said that sustained exposure to anti-LGBTI content on Facebook caused them anxiety, frustration and feelings of helplessness even in cases where they reported the harmful content. “Facebook is just another piece in the pile of my anxiety... to them (Meta) users are not people, they are just numbers,” one interviewee told Amnesty International. Some interviewees temporarily withdrew from the platform and participation in public discussions to protect their mental health. Others self-censored fearing a backlash if they openly expressed their sexual orientation, gender identity, or support for the rights of LGBTI people on the platform. These experiences raise concerns over whether Facebook failed to protect the rights to freedom of expression and non-discrimination, by undermining LGBTI people’s ability to participate in public and civic life on an equal basis with others. “Over the last decade, members of the Hungarian LGBTI community faced severe smear campaigns and repressive laws from the Orbán government. They also could not express themselves freely on Meta platforms which largely added to their despair” – said Eszter Mihály, LGBTI rights officer at Amnesty Hungary. Facebook’s central role in debates As part of the research, Amnesty International also conducted a social listening exercise of public discourse on LGBTI issues across various social media platforms. We found that discussions concerning LGBTI people were characterized by fearmongering, misinformation, and derogatory rhetoric, with Facebook serving as a central forum for these debates. Representatives of Háttér Society , a Hungarian organization that supports and advocates for the rights of LGBTI people, shared with Amnesty examples of harmful content on Facebook identified between January 2023 and December 2024. They included comments calling for physical violence against LGBTI people, with statements such as “Beat them to death immediately”, “I would shoot this”, “Throw them off the bridge”, and “Death to the extreme genderfluid vermin”. Other comments used dehumanizing language, referring to LGBTI people as “rats”, “mutants”, “earthworms” or “scum”, while some explicitly advocated the eradication of transgender people. Several other examples pushed narratives portraying LGBTI people as threats to children, public morality, or social order. Some harmful content remained accessible for a period of time after being reported, including content that was still available when checked in March 2026. The continued availability of such content indicates ongoing shortcomings in the consistency and effectiveness of Meta’s enforcement systems. Interviewees repeatedly encountered anti-LGBTI content despite actively seeking to avoid it by blocking accounts, reporting harmful content, and communicating their disinterest to Facebook. “Now my feed is really unhealthy. It is not just one or two videos: it’s a series of videos. Now I only can see that. There is rarely any content from friends. Ádám Kanicsár, an LGBTI activist and journalist, told Amnesty International Other interviewees also noted that they were shown content they were not interested in. “Taken together, these findings raise concerns that Facebook’s design may also have increased users’ exposure to harmful anti-LGBTI content. The findings suggest that engagement-driven systems may be contributing to repeated exposure to harmful and divisive content,” said Alia Al Ghussain, the Head of Amnesty International’s Big Tech Accountability Team. Under the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA), Meta is required to identify and prevent systemic risks related to platform design to ensure that its products are not causing or contributing to human rights abuses. The company must reassess the impact of its January 2025 policy changes in different contexts, and strengthen content moderation and enforcement. This includes an effective complaint mechanism, improve transparency on the enforcements and effectiveness of its policies and the provision of effective remedies to those affected by any harms. The European Commission must robustly enforce the DSA and investigate Meta’s compliance with its obligations. Amnesty International wrote to Meta on 28 July sharing its conclusions. On 11 August, Meta replied stating that, given the scope and detail of the findings presented, it could not share a response within the stipulated timeline. Background The research was conducted amid a worsening environment for LGBTI rights in Hungary. Under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, the government introduced discriminatory laws and policies with government aligned actors portraying LGBTI people as threats to children, families, and Hungarian values. These trends intensified in 2025 and 2026 with new laws restricting LGBTI related gatherings, including Pride events.

https://www.amnesty.org/en/annual-report.body: Amnesty has been producing its annual report on human rights for over 60 years. We cover many countries and focus on key human rights issues with full or partial versions available in many languages. It is a valuable free resource for anyone interested in human rights. Find out below what is included in the reports, how to access each edition and how the report can be used to help support human rights . What is included Each edition includes key human rights developments at a national, regional and global level. They cover a full calendar year, now running from 1 January to 31 December, with individual entries on around 150 or so countries (the exact number varies from year to year), plus global and regional analysis of key human rights concerns. Reports offer a broad overview of the state of the word’s human rights. Country entries feature specific concerns. Regional overviews draw out the key themes at a regional level, and our global analysis focuses on a selection of significant trends spanning different regions. How to access current and past editions All annual reports are available in PDF format. Individual country entries in the most recent annual reports are also available as HTML web pages. You can click on the quick links [below] to find an archive of our annual reports and you can download free PDF copies of the reports there. We no longer supply printed copies. Using to support human rights Amnesty’s annual report is a unique free source of reference on human rights across the world and aimed at a wide audience. Journalists use it for background on the human rights situation on countries on which they are reporting, lawyers use it to support asylum claims for refugees, human rights advocates use it as a tool to pressure governments, academics use it to analyse human rights trends over decades and diplomats use it to inform foreign policy discussions. In fact, anyone with an interest in human rights at home or internationally will find Amnesty’s annual report a useful resource. “What I find most useful about this rich resource is the clear and simple language, which is a breath of fresh air compared to many academic writings on the same subject. The unbiased and well-referenced details are helpful in building a background picture of the situation in any country.” PhD student Disambiguation Although we still use the term “annual report”, this annual publication is neither a report of its financial statements and accounts nor a report focused primarily on Amnesty’s own activities. The annual report on the affairs of the Amnesty International Charity together with its financial statements and auditors’ report can be found on our finance page . https://www.amnesty.org/en/cookie-statem.body: Amnesty International’s website, like most websites, uses small text files called cookies. This note provides information on what cookies are, which cookies Amnesty International uses, and how they can be controlled. If you wish to restrict or block cookies you can set your internet browser to do so- click on the following link for further information: www.aboutcookies.org 1. What are cookies? Cookies are text files containing small amounts of information which are downloaded to your device when you visit a website. Cookies are then sent back to the originating website on each subsequent visit, or to another website that recognises that cookie. Cookies are widely used because they allow a website to recognise a user’s device and therefore allow enhanced functionality. You can find out more information about cookies at: www.allaboutcookies.org some definitions used in this note are provided at part 5 below. 2. How does Amnesty International use cookies? Amnesty International uses cookies for the following purposes: to compile statistical data on the use of our website and its functioning, so that we can monitor and improve it; to facilitate users’ ability to navigate through our website, including allowing registered users to access secure parts of our website; to allow us to optimize our advertising on 3rd party advertising platforms such as social media; and to allow us to reduce malicious traffic to donation pages. 3. Which cookies does Amnesty International use? A full list of all the cookies we use is in the table in part 6 below. Please note that some cookies can be set by 3rd party content providers in content that is embedded in our site. We are auditing the use of all cookies and the table will be updated as we make ongoing changes. 4. How to control cookies If you do not wish to receive cookies you can set your web browser to restrict or block them. All modern browsers allow you to change your cookie settings, typically be found in the ‘options’ or ‘preferences’ menu of your browser. In order to understand these settings, the following link may be helpful: www.aboutcookies.org If you disable cookies you will not be able to use all the interactive features of our website. 5. Definitions First Party/ Third party cookies Refers to the web domain placing the cookie. First-party cookies are those set by a website that is being visited by the user at the time – the website displayed in the URL window. Third party cookies are cookies that are set by a domain other than that of the website being visited by the user. If a user visits a website and another entity sets the cookie through that website, this would be a third-party cookie. Persistent cookies These cookies remain on a user’s device for the period of time specified in the cookie. They are activated each time that the user visits the website that created that particular cookie. Session cookies These cookies allow website operators to link the actions of a user during a browser session. A browser session starts when a user opens the browser window and finishes when they close the browser window. Session cookies are created temporarily. Once you close the browser, all session cookies are deleted. Pixel tags A pixel tag is not technically a cookie but is a similar type of technology placed on a website or within the body of an email for the purpose of tracking activity on websites, or when emails are opened or accessed, and is often used in combination with cookies. Information collected is anonymous. 6. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/26.body: Listen (6 mins) Save Share ‘Freeze the conflict’: Drones slow Kazakh oil flow amid Russia-Ukraine war on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google An interior view shows a pumping station of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which accounts for about 80 percent of Kazakhstan's oil exports [File: Mariya Gordeyeva/Reuters] By Mansur Mirovalev Published On 26 Jul 2026 26 Jul 2026 Sitting next to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on Saturday cautiously weighed in on the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year. “If I may offer my humble opinion ... perhaps it is time to freeze this conflict and return to the Istanbul formula 2.0,” he told reporters in the ⁠Siberian city of Omsk. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 At least 15 killed in Ukrainian and Russian strikes as holiday camp hit list 2 of 3 Ukraine war: Is Kazakhstan going cool on Russia? list 3 of 3 Iran accuses Ukraine of deadly attack on Caspian commercial vessel end of list Tokayev was referring to a botched agreement that envisaged an immediate suspension of hostilities along the existing front line and further talks brokered by Western powers. After Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow ally Tokayev dared to contradict Putin by emphasising that Kazakhstan would not recognise occupied Ukrainian regions as part of Russia. But this time, he praised Putin’s “diplomatic flexibility” and named Russia among the “great powers” that could guarantee peace in Ukraine. “All of this should be stopped, because what’s happening plays into the hands of the enemies of Russia and the Ukrainian people,” said Tokayev. Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. left, and Russian counterpartVladimir Putin speak at they attend the 22nd Russia-Kazakhstan Forum of Interregional Cooperation in Omsk on July 25 [AFP] His comments came as Kazakhstan, a country boasting several “supergiant” oil fields that serve as the European Union’s second-largest source of crude, said on Thursday that it had slashed oil production after drone attacks blamed on Ukraine forced its main export terminal on the Black Sea to shut down. Light but “sour”, or hard to process, Kazakhstan’s crude is known as the CPC brand, named after the Caspian Pipeline Consortium that includes Western energy giants such as Chevron, ExxonMobil and Shell. Advertisement The pipeline that pumps the crude westwards across the bone-dry steppes is 1,500km (932 miles) long and ends in the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk. The port is said to have become the new hideout for Russia’s Black Sea Fleet that fled the annexed Crimea Peninsula after hundreds of Ukrainian attacks by aerial and sea drones and missiles following the start of the war. Novorossiisk is also the target of Ukraine’s new policy of striking Moscow’s “shadow fleet” of tankers that ship Russian oil despite Western sanctions. In recent weeks, Ukrainian drones have hit almost 200 “shadow fleet” vessels, including tankers and dry cargo ships, in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. Drone attacks that Kazakhstan blames on Ukraine have also struck several tankers with CPC oil and damaged the consortium’s marine terminal in Novorossiysk. ‘Unacceptable encroachment’ The attacks, which began in November 2025 but intensified this month, prompted an angry response from officials in Kazakhstan’s capital, Astana. In a statement on July 19, the Foreign Ministry called them an “unacceptable encroachment” on Kazakhstan’s economic interests, saying they were designed to “destabilise legitimate international trade, world energy markets, and the security of global transport and logistics supply chains”. A day later, Ukraine’s Ambassador to Kazakhstan Viktor Mayko retorted by saying that there was “no proof” that the drones were Ukrainian and that Astana should refrain from “hasty and ungrounded accusations”. By Thursday, the CPC “temporarily suspended” oil shipments – and would only renew them after “the situation is normalised”, the Kazakh Energy Ministry said. With oil and gas accounting for about a fifth of its gross domestic product, Kazakhstan is rightly concerned as 80 percent of its oil exports are at risk. “This is a direct strike on the economy and budget,” regional expert Daniil Kislov told Al Jazeera. To some average Kazakhs worried about galloping inflation and rising prices, the disruption of oil exports seems like the least of their worries – just like the Russia-Ukraine war that triggered it. “I don’t care, because the money doesn’t reach me anyway,” Alzhas, a bank clerk in Almaty, Kazakhstan’s business capital, told Al Jazeera, withholding his last name because of security concerns. He said that people around him “stopped talking, arguing about the war, since there’s only one question about how to earn money for food, and the rest about Russia and Ukraine is irrelevant”. EU member states that largely depend on Kazakh crude are also concerned. Advertisement Romania tops the list, getting more than 60 percent of its crude from Kazakhstan and then processing it domestically. Interim Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan on Thursday tried to dissuade Romanians from panicking, saying the government did not expect “there to be any supply problems”. He added, however, that a drop in gasoline production of up to 15 percent is expected if Kazakhstan does not resume shipments. Experts say the long-term outlook, especially for Kazakhstan, is bleak. Kyiv-based analyst Aleksey Kusch said that if the disruptions go on, more Kazakh oil will have to be directed at a higher cost to a pipeline that crosses the Caspian into Azerbaijan – and this could eventually lead to the “loss of oil revenues”. Volodymyr Fesenko, head of the Kyiv-based Penta think tank, described the situation as “uneasy and controversial”, noting that there might be “informal pressure” on Ukraine from the White House since US oil companies have stakes in the Kazakh oil fields. There could be “persistent recommendations to Ukrainian President [Volodomyr] Zelenskyy not to touch this very terminal in Novorossiisk,” he said, predicting, however, that there would not be “any cardinal, fatal, negative consequences” for Kyiv. “They will try to solve it behind closed doors, unofficially,” he said. And by some accounts, the US did step in. Chevron Chief Executive Mike Wirth approached White House officials earlier this week to solve the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday. An unnamed US official told the Journal that the administration of US President Donald Trump warned Ukraine against attacking non-Russian ships in the Black Sea.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/6.body: Save Share Kazakhstan, which already recognises Israel, to join ‘Abraham Accords’ on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev speaks during the 80th United Nations General Assembly in New York City, on September 23 [Jeenah Moon/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff Published On 6 Nov 2025 6 Nov 2025 More than 33 years after establishing official diplomatic ties with Israel, Kazakhstan says it will join the so-called Abraham Accords , which formalised ties between Israel and several Arab countries. The announcement came on Thursday ahead of a meeting between United States President Donald Trump and the leaders of Central Asian countries. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Trump says he was ‘very much in charge’ of Israel’s June 13 attack on Iran list 2 of 3 SOAS University ‘concerned’ by reports of Sami Hamdi’s detention in the US list 3 of 3 Dutch court rejects bid to halt arms exports to Israel over Gaza war end of list “Our anticipated accession to the Abraham Accords represents a natural and logical continuation of Kazakhstan’s foreign policy course – grounded in dialogue, mutual respect, and regional stability,” Kazakhstan’s government said in a statement, according to the AFP news agency. Earlier in the day, US envoy for the Middle East Steve Witkoff had announced that another country would join the normalisation deals without identifying it. “Abraham Accords are big. I’m flying back to Washington tonight because we’re going to announce, tonight, another country coming into the Abraham Accords,” Witkoff said. It is not clear how joining the accords will affect the already established Kazakh-Israeli ties. The countries established diplomatic relations in 1992, shortly after Kazakhstan gained independence from the Soviet Union. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Kazakhstan in 2016, and the two countries have several bilateral agreements. The announcement comes at a time when Trump is promoting himself as a peacemaker after brokering the tenuous ceasefire in Gaza, despite the daily deadly Israeli violence against Palestinians and the escalation of Israeli attacks in Lebanon . Kazakhstan appears to be pushing to deepen its ties with the US as its President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev visits Washington. On Thursday, the two countries signed a cooperation deal over critical minerals. Advertisement During his first term, Trump brokered the Abraham Accords, a series of deals that formalised ties between Arab countries – the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Morocco – and Israel. The push shattered Arab states’ consensus over the 2002 Arab Peace Initiative, which conditioned recognition of Israel on the establishment of a viable Palestinian state. Netanyahu has categorically rejected that “land for peace” framework, pushing instead for deals with Arab countries that bypass Palestinians . Former President Joe Biden, who succeeded Trump, made expanding the deals a priority in his approach to the Middle East early on. But the agreements – brokered between countries that were never at war – did little to resolve the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians and the decades-long occupation that leading rights groups say amounts to a system of apartheid . Still, the normalisation deals withstood the two-year war in Gaza, which saw Israel flatten much of the territory and kill more than 68,800 Palestinians. The UAE and other countries involved in the agreements have maintained their trade and security ties with Israel. In recent months, Trump has repeatedly said he hopes that Saudi Arabia will join the accords. But Saudi officials have stressed their commitment to the Arab Peace Initiative.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/31.body: Listen (2 mins) Save Share Kazakhstan’s Tokayev appoints longtime adviser as vice president on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attends the Supreme Eurasian Economic Union summit in Astana, Kazakhstan, Friday, May 29, 2026 [Alexander Kazakov/Kremlin Pool Photo via AP] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 31 Aug 2026 31 Aug 2026 Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed longtime adviser Erlan Karin as vice president, the office created under a new constitution adopted earlier this year. The move on Monday makes Karin, who has served as a top ⁠⁠aide to Tokayev since taking over the presidency in 2019, first in line to succeed him as leader of the Central Asian country. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Kazakhstan’s newly formed pro-government party wins parliamentary election list 2 of 4 Kazakhstan releases first tiger to restore extinct species list 3 of 4 Kazakhstan parliamentary elections begin: What’s at stake? list 4 of 4 Tokayev allies head for landslide victory in Kazakhstan elections end of list Tokayev described Karin as an experienced public servant with extensive knowledge of state governance, local media reported. “He has worked in the system of public administration for many years. One can say that he is a person of broad outlook, with rich experience and a true patriot,” Tokayev was quoted as saying. The 50-year-old has a background in “counter-terrorism” and has ⁠⁠positioned himself as a key figure in promoting Tokayev’s ideology, which he has dubbed “New Kazakhstan”. Tokayev also proposed reappointing Olzhas Bektenov as prime minister, a position ⁠⁠he has held since 2024. Both appointments were swiftly approved by parliament, which is dominated ⁠⁠by the pro-Tokayev Adilet party. Tokayev, 73, is eligible to run for another seven-year term as president under the new constitution, according to Kazakhstan’s supreme court. His current term ends in 2029. presidents are otherwise limited to a single term in office under Kazakh basic law. Tokayev, a ⁠⁠former Soviet diplomat and top United Nations official, took office as the chosen successor of Nursultan Nazarbayev, Kazakhstan’s founding president, who ruled from 1991 to 2019. Advertisement Tokayev broke from his predecessor, whom he had served as prime minister and foreign minister, in 2022 after a bout of nationwide unrest that left hundreds dead and which he cast as a coup attempt by Nazarbayev-era figures. Kazakhstan is a major exporter of energy and minerals, including uranium for nuclear power, and maintains warm ties with Russia, the West and China.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/23.body: Listen (2 mins) Save Share Polls close in Kazakhstan parliamentary elections; vote count under way on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google People vote at a polling station during snap parliamentary elections in Almaty, Kazakhstan, on August 23, 2026 [Pavel Mikheyev/Reuters] By AFP and Reuters Published On 23 Aug 2026 23 Aug 2026 Polls have closed in Kazakhstan’s snap parliamentary elections, which are expected to further strengthen the power of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Voting concluded on Sunday at 8pm (03:00 GMT), and Central Election Commission officials began counting ballots. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Kazakhstan parliamentary elections begin: What’s at stake? list 2 of 4 Ukraine’s Zelenskyy set to meet Trump as Iran and Ukraine wars converge list 3 of 4 Kazakhstan releases first tiger to restore extinct species list 4 of 4 Ukraine’s 40-day campaign has not brought the war closer to an end end of list According to the commission, 74 percent of about 12 million eligible voters cast their votes to choose a new single-chamber, 145-member parliament called the Kurultai. The pro-Tokayev Adilet party is widely predicted to win an overwhelming majority, according to The Associated Press news agency, and several smaller parties loyal to Tokayev are also expected to enter parliament. Sunday’s vote was the culmination of a constitutional overhaul that Tokayev initiated in March when 87 percent of voters supported a referendum to abolish Kazakhstan’s upper house in favour of a unicameral parliament. Officials said the change would give parliament more weight in political decision-making, having previously been confined to a mostly auxiliary role. However, only seven state-approved parties, all loyal to Tokayev, have been allowed to put forth candidates. The constitutional changes also reset term limits to allow Tokayev to run again in 2029. He has led the Central Asian country since 2019. The 73-year-old was the chosen successor of longtime leader Nursultan Nazarbayev , who ruled for almost 30 years from the 1990s. But Tokayev broke with his predecessor amid cost-of-living protests in 2022 that led to the deaths of 238 people and has since touted a reform agenda called “Just Kazakhstan”. Advertisement The election came at a difficult economic moment for Kazakhstan as inflation hit 10.2 percent in February and tax hikes have fuelled public discontent. The vote also took place against a backdrop of intensifying crackdowns on media freedom. Media organisations have urged Tokayev to drop criminal charges against several journalists under house arrest and to revise legislation to ensure media freedom. Authorities have opened roughly 10 criminal cases against independent journalists and popular bloggers. A former Soviet state, Kazakhstan balances relations with China, Europe and Russia, and Tokayev has had to navigate recent tensions over Moscow’s war with Ukraine. Kazakhstan is oil-rich and produces about 2 percent of the world’s daily supply, mostly exporting to European countries through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium to Russia’s port of Novorossiysk. Tokayev, who has sought to maintain a delicate balance between Moscow and the West since sanctions were imposed on Russia over the war in Ukraine, has justified the constitutional changes by citing the need for rapid decision-making in a fast-changing world.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/24.body: Listen (7 mins) Save Share Ukraine’s offensive against Russia causes petrol panic across Central Asia on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Cossacks keep order at a petrol station and prevent conflicts due to fuel shortages in the Russian Black Sea resort of Anapa, July 8, 2026 [Sergey Pivovarov/Reuters] By Mansur Mirovalev Published On 24 Aug 2026 24 Aug 2026 A Russian woman explained on camera what made her and a smiling, bearded man next to her drive to a petrol station in Kazakhstan. “Simply to fill the tank,” she said in a viral video that explains new terms in today’s Russia: “fuel tourism” and “gas hunting”. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 ‘Long-range sanctions’: Ukraine hopes strikes cause Russia fear and losses list 2 of 4 ‘New level of danger’: Drone incidents scare Europe amid Russia-Ukraine war list 3 of 4 Russian expert warns of impending social crisis as Ukraine death toll rises list 4 of 4 How China and Russia could hobble Trump’s plans to isolate Iran end of list For most of this year, swarms of Ukrainian drones have been burning down Russian oil refineries and fuel depots from annexed Crimea to the Baltic to western Siberia, causing sky-high plumes of putrid smoke. As Russian President Vladimir Putin refuses to resume peace talks, claiming that his forces “advance in all directions”, tens of millions of Russians face fuel shortages and hours-long queues at petrol stations – with occasional shouting and fist fights. And those living in regions bordering Kazakhstan – including a string of urban centres along the Volga River, Russia’s most densely populated region – drive to Central Asia’s most oil-rich nation, often hundreds of kilometres, just to fill up. Even though in late May the Kazakh government banned petrol exports, border guards report thwarting hundreds of attempts to smuggle fuel back to Russia in canisters, makeshift fuel tanks – or in giant fuel trucks. But some industrious smugglers still make their way across the world’s second-longest land border that stretches 7,644km (4,750 miles) across the barren steppe, according to people interviewed for this article. “There’s total contraband along the border,” Timur, a businessman in Almaty, Kazakhstan’s capital, told Al Jazeera. He withheld his last name for safety reasons. Advertisement Even though Kazakhstan boasts three giant, Soviet-era oil refineries, fuel prices in Kazakhstan increased by 15.6 percent this year, the UlusMedia website reported on July 10 . Only one of Kazakhstan’s neighbours, Turkmenistan, has large hydrocarbon reserves, but its autocratic leaders isolated the country from the rest of the region in the 1990s. ‘Deficit here for a long time’ Other Central Asian nations feel the ripple effect too – especially Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, resource-poor, mountainous nations that used to get up to 90 percent of their petrol from Russia. “They’ve been hurt the most,” Galiya Ibragimova, a Moldova-based expert on Central Asia with Carnegie Politika, which is headquartered in Berlin, told Al Jazeera. Kyrgyzstan is a member of the Eurasian Economic Union, the free trade bloc of five former Soviet nations dominated by Russia and the Kremlin’s political decisions. Tajikistan is not a member of the group, but it bought discounted Russian fuel as “payment for political loyalty, not because Putin is so kind”, Ibragimova said. A key source of petrol for Central Asia was Russia’s largest refinery in the city of Omsk in southwestern Siberia. But it stopped operating after Ukrainian drone attacks in early July that damaged a crude distillation unit. Around that time, Kyrgyzstan began regulating petrol prices and asked other ex-Soviet nations for help to “ensure sustainable fuel supplies”. Kyrgyz experts predict long-term problems at Russian refineries will take months or even years to fix. “Equipment for oil refineries is not a delivery from an online shop or a supermarket,” Kyrgyz energy expert Olzhas Baydildinov said in televised remarks. “The deficit that has come is here for a long time.” The Kyrgyz government pledged to “provide at least a half” of Kyrgyzstan’s needs – but only after modernising the nation’s largest refinery, deputy energy minister Nasipbek Kerimov said in early July. He did not specify how long it would take. By the middle of this month, Kyrgyz authorities said they had spent about $11.4m to subsidise petrol prices. China’s help in drilling Tajikistan is especially vulnerable because domestic oil processing amounts to 0.5 percent of petrol consumed there. Drivers already face fuel shortages and limits of 20 litres per car at some petrol stations. “There are problems both in the [processing of oil] and in logistics,” deputy energy minister Daler Juma said in early July, when announcing that the government had amassed fuel reserves that would last “at least 60 days”. Advertisement In mid-August, he travelled to Tehran and signed a deal to provide 2.5 million tonnes of oil, petrol and diesel from Iran. With the help of experts from the giant state-owned China National Petroleum Corporation, Tajikistan has intensified the search for prospective oil fields. By the end of this year, they are due to submit a report on seismic reconnaissance, a method of quickly assessing potential oil reserves. “Then, we will decide where we can start drilling,” Tajikistan’s chief geologist, Ilhomjon Oymukhammadzoda, told a news conference in early July. Uzbekistan’s ‘reserves’ for winter Both Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan used to resell Russian petrol to neighbouring Uzbekistan, the regional economic powerhouse with a population of almost 39 million and half a dozen car manufacturing companies. As Uzbekistan processes its own oil into petrol satisfying about two-thirds of its needs, the rest usually comes from Russia. But the new shortages have forced the government to start amassing a strategic reserve. “We have a separate plan for the fall and winter, we’ve created enough reserves. I can say with confidence that we have enough reserves for two or three months,” deputy energy minister, Umid Mamadaminov, said early last month. Meanwhile, many Uzbek drivers are happy they switched their engines to run on compressed natural gas – even though huge gas tanks take up most of the boot. “I switched 15 years ago, saved a lot of money,” Azamat Tolipov, a taxi driver in the Uzbek capital, Tashkent, told Al Jazeera. Regional governments are trying to find new sources of oil and gas, but the United States and Israeli war on Iran drives global prices up. “Central Asian nations will convulsively look for new suppliers, but considering what’s going on in the Strait of Hormuz , even if they find an alternative, it will be more expensive,” analyst Ibragimova predicted. Beijing seems to be the only power to benefit from the fuel crisis as sales of Chinese-made electric cars skyrocketed even before it unfolded. Electric car sales in Kazakhstan alone grew 36 times between 2022 and 2025, said the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center, a Berlin-based think tank in last year’s report titled: “China has flooded Central Asia with electric cars”.

Listen (3 mins) Save Share Kazakhstan’s newly formed pro-government party wins parliamentary election on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Electoral commission staff in Almaty count parliamentary election votes after polling stations closed after Sunday's election [Pavel Mikheyev/Reuters] By AFP and Reuters Published On 24 Aug 2026 24 Aug 2026 Kazakhstan’s pro-government Adilet party won more than 71 percent of the vote in Sunday’s parliamentary election , said the electoral commission in a result likely to consolidate the power of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev . Announcing the results on Monday, the commission said that four other blocs also entered parliament: the pro-business Respublika and Ak Zhol parties, the centre-left Nationwide Social Democratic Party and the Auyl party, which represents rural voters. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Pakistan’s army chief back in Iran: Can he break peace talks deadlock? list 2 of 3 Ukraine’s allies convene in Kyiv as Zelenskyy seeks air defence boost list 3 of 3 How much more are you spending on petrol since the war on Iran began? end of list According to the commission, 74 percent of eligible voters cast ballots to choose the new 145-member, single-chamber parliament, called the Kurultai. Approximately 12.6 million of the 20 million population were eligible to vote. Adilet was founded in the Central Asian nation earlier this year and is led by Tokayev’s top aides. Shortly after its inception, it absorbed the previous ruling party, Amanat. All four other parties entering parliament are also seen as broadly supportive of Tokayev’s administration. Sunday’s election was triggered by a new constitution adopted earlier this year, which streamlined parliament from two chambers into one. Kazakhstan’s Supreme Court ruled last month that the new constitution allows Tokayev to run for a new seven-year term. Officials say that the structural change aims to give parliament more weight in political decision-making. Previously, it was confined to a largely auxiliary role under a system that concentrated power in the presidency. A former Soviet diplomat and top United Nations official, Tokayev has led Central Asia’s largest economy since 2019, maintaining warm relations with the West, Russia and China. Advertisement Tokayev has also championed a reform programme called “Just Kazakhstan”. The initiative followed riots in 2022 when 238 people were killed as cost-of-living protests escalated. The 73-year-old president said he is trying to move away from the legacy of his authoritarian predecessor, Nursultan Nazarbayev , who ruled for three decades after the collapse of the Soviet Union. Tokayev originally took office as the chosen successor of Nazarbayev, Kazakhstan’s founding president, who governed from 1991 to 2019. While voting in the capital, Astana, Tokayev told journalists it was too early to say whether he would seek another term. He also said that he would name his choice for vice president, the newly created office under the new constitution, within the next seven to 10 days, adding that it would be a “well-known” person.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/20.body: Listen (4 mins) Save Share Indonesia, Morocco, Kosovo among 5 countries to send troops under Gaza plan on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Video Duration 02 minutes 27 seconds 02:27 Trump announces billions of dollars in Gaza aid at Board of Peace meeting By Lyndal Rowlands Published On 20 Feb 2026 20 Feb 2026 Indonesia, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Kosovo and Albania have pledged to send troops to Gaza, the commander of a newly created International Stabilization Force (ISF) has said during a meeting of United States President Donald Trump’s so-called Board of Peace. US Army General Jasper Jeffers, who has been appointed as the head of a future Gaza stabilisation force by Trump’s board, said on Thursday that the Indonesian contingent to the mission has “accepted the position of deputy commander”. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Trump’s Board of Peace meets: Who’s in, who’s out, what’s on the agenda? list 2 of 4 Diplomats slam Israel’s Gaza ‘ceasefire’ violations, West Bank push at UNSC list 3 of 4 What can Trump achieve as ‘Board of Peace’ meets for the first time? list 4 of 4 Trump announces billions of dollars in Gaza aid at Board of Peace meeting end of list “With these first steps, we will help bring the security that Gaza needs,” Jeffers said during a meeting of the board in Washington, DC. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, who was among several world leaders participating in the meeting, said his country would contribute up to 8,000 personnel to the planned force “to make this peace work” in the war-torn Palestinian territory, where Israel’s genocide has killed at least 72,000 people. Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said his country will also send an unspecified number of troops, including medical units, to Gaza, while Morocco’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita said that his country is ready to deploy police officers to Gaza. Albania, whose prime minister recently made a two-day official visit to Israel, has also said it will contribute troops, while neighbouring countries Egypt and Jordan have said they will participate by training police officers. Indonesia, which was one of the first countries to commit to sending troops, has sought to reassure potential critics that its participation is intended to ensure international law is upheld in Gaza, amid Israel’s genocidal onslaught. Advertisement ‘Indonesian troops will not be involved in combat operations’ Indonesia’s foreign minister met with both United Nations chief Antonio Guterres and Palestinian ambassador to the UN Riyad Mansour in New York on Wednesday, in advance of President Subianto’s participation in the Board of Peace meeting. “Indonesia’s mandate [on troop deployment] is humanitarian in nature with a focus on protecting civilians, humanitarian and health assistance, reconstruction as well as training and strengthening the capacity of the Palestinian Police,” Indonesia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a recent statement, according to the Jakarta Post newspaper. “Indonesian troops will not be involved in combat operations or any action leading to direct confrontation with any armed group,” the ministry said, responding to questions raised over its future role in Gaza by Amnesty International. The head of Amnesty International Indonesia, Usman Hamid, has voiced concerns that Indonesia risked violating international law through its participation in the Board of Peace and the planned stabilisation force for Gaza. Hamid warned that Indonesia’s deployment of troops to Gaza “means putting Indonesia at risk of participating in a mechanism that will strengthen violations of International Humanitarian Law”. “The Peace Council does not include members from the most disadvantaged Palestinians, but instead includes members from Israel, which has for nearly eight decades carried out an illegal occupation and apartheid against the Palestinian people, even committing genocide in Gaza,” Hamid wrote last week in an open letter to the speaker of the People’s Representative Council of the Republic of Indonesia. Palestinians have also voiced concerns that Trump’s Board of Peace will only further entrench Israel’s illegal occupation of the Gaza Strip, as Israeli forces continue to carve out more “buffer zones” and restrict the entry of food and other aid, months into a so-called “ceasefire” with Hamas, during which almost 600 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks. The Gaza stabilisation force differs from other peacekeeping forces deployed by multilateral organisations such as the UN or the African Union. In neighbouring Lebanon, more than 10,000 peacekeepers from 47 countries continue to participate in the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) , which was created in 1978. Indonesia, along with Italy, is one of the largest contributors of troops to UNIFIL, which has repeatedly come under fire from Israeli forces , despite a fragile ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

https://www.azattyq.org/a/resei-drondary.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Ресей дрондары Польшаға жақын аумақты соққылады. Украина Мәскеу "НАТО есігін қақты" деп ескертті 13 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 17:16 Ресей дрондары Польшаға жақын аумақты соққылады. Украина Мәскеу "НАТО есігін қақты" деп ескертті Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Ресей әскерінің Украинадағы пойыздарға шабуылы. Қазан айы, 2025 жыл. Ресейлік екі дрон 13 қыркүйекте Польша шекарасына жақын аумақты соққылады, Украина билігі Мәскеу "ЕО мен НАТО-ның есігін қақты" деп мәлімдеп, санкцияны күшейтуге шақырды. Ресейлік дрон жексенбі күні күндіз Польша мен Украина арасындағы Ягодин жанармай станциясына соққы жасады. Зардап шеккендер туралы мәлімет жоқ. Украинаның Волын облысындағы шекара бекеті жабылып, қайта ашылды. Волында сонымен бірге ресейлік дрон Польша шекарасынан екі шақырым жердегі жолаушылар пойызы локомотивіне соққы жасады деп хабарлады Украина темір жолы. Олардың айтынша, мониторинг топтары пойыздың қызметкерлеріне қатер жөнінде алдын ала ескертіп үлгерген. Видеода халықтың темір жол станциясында жарылыс болған аумақтан қашып жатқаны көрінеді. Сол жақтағы көлік қызметкері Олександр Шевченконың сөзінше, ресейлік дрон Варшавадан Киевке келе жатқан пойыз локомотивіне 13 қыркүйекте таңертең соққы жасаған. Зардап шеккендер туралы ақпарат жарияланбады. Мұндай соққы Ресей Украинадағы азаматтық инфрақұрылым нысандарына шабуылын күшейткен тұста жасалды. Сонымен қатар ЕО өкілдері Ресейдің Еуропа елдерінің әуе кеңістігін бұзу әрекеттері жиілеп, мұндай жағдай «қалыпты құбылысқа» айналып бара жатқанын ескерткен кезде жасалды. "Ресейдің Украина-Польша шекарасындағы Ягодинге варварлық шабуылдары шекарамызға жасалған соққылардың жалғасы ғана емес. Бұл ЕО мен НАТО-ның "есігін тіке қаққан" Путиннің терроры" деп жазды Украина сыртқы істер министрі Андрей Сибига X желісінде. Ол Еуропа басшыларын Ресейге қарсы санкцияны күшейтуге шақырды. "Мәскеу террорының салдарын сезінсін. Жарым-жартылай шешім емес, ымырасыз, қуатты қадамдар [керек]. Тұтас саудаға эмбарго. Кіруге толық тыйым. Әскери-өнеркәсіп кешеніне қарсы толық санкция" деді ол. Осы айдың басында Германияда жарылғыш заттары бар дрон Лейпциг әуежайының жұмысын тоқтатқан кезде Берлин оқиғаға Мәскеуді ресми түрде айыптаған. Еурокомиссияның басшысы Урсула фон дер Ляйен мұның қалыпты құбылысқа айналып бара жатқанын айтқан. Украина президенті 13 қыркүйекте Ресей өткен аптада Украинаға аумағына жалпы 1200 дрон, 1700 қанатты бомба, 73 ракета ұшырғанын айтқан. "Бұл соққының әрі қарай Еуропаға жайылуына жол бермес үшін украин ерлері мен әйелдері күн сайын күресіп, өмірлерін қиып жатыр" деп жазды Телеграм-парақшасында. Руслан МЕДЕЛБЕК 13 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 16:47 "Корттағы машина әлі талай титул жеңеді". Рыбакинаның жеңісі жайлы халықаралық басылымдар не жазды? Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Елена Рыбакина US Open турнирінің кубогымен. 12 қыркүйек 2026 жыл. Қазақстан теннисшісі Елена Рыбакина Grand Slam турнирлері қатарына енетін US Open жарысында жеңіске жетті. Қазақстандық 27 жастағы теннисшінің жеңісі жайлы әлемдік БАҚ не жазып жатыр? Шолып шықтық. "РЫБАКИНА - ӘМБЕБАП ОЙЫНШЫ" Британиялық ВВС сайты "Рыбакина Нью-Йорктен US Open чемпионы атағымен әрі әлемнің жаңа бірінші ракеткасы ретінде кетіп барады" деп жазды. Қазақстан теннисшісі Нью-Йоркте өткен финалда Арина Соболенконы (Беларусь) үш сетте жеңді – 6:4, 5:7, 6:2. Осылайша Рыбакина әлемдік рейтингіде Соболенконы екінші орынға ығыстырып, бірінші орынға шықты. ВВС басылымының теннис сарапшылар Рыбакинаның кортта мүлде эмоция көрсетпейтінін, жеңіліп жатса да, жеңсе де бірқалыпты болатынына баса назар аударған. Мәселен британиялық экс-теннисші Аннабель Крофт ВВС радиосының эфирінде "Рыбакина кортта өте салқынқанды. Ойын кезінде мүлде эмоция көрсетпейтіні таңдай қақтырады. Рыбакина кортта құдды бір машина сияқты. Оның не ойлап жүргенін, ойында не бар екенін ешкім білмейді" деді. Елена Рыбакина US Open финалында. 12 қыркүйек 2026 жыл. Ал тағы бір британиялық экс-теннисші Лора Робсон Sky Sports телеарнасының эфирінде "Рыбакина – кез келген төсеніште (теннис корттары хард, грунд және шөп деп үшке бөлінеді – Азаттық.) әмбебап ойыншы. Грунт оның ойынына сәл келмейді, бірақ тез, динамикасы жоғары корттарда Рыбакинаны тоқтату қиын. Ол алда әлі де Grand Slam жарыстарын жеңетініне сенемін. Хард кортта ол доп асыруы мен доп қабылдауы мықты болса қарсылас шақ келтірмейді" дейді. Аннабель Крофт ВВС радиосында "Рыбакинаның өкшесін басып келе жатқан қарсыластары көп. Кейде оның ойынында төмендеу болады, бірақ ең маңызды сәттерде ол мықты ойнайтынын көрсетті" деп бағалады. Қазақстан теннишісі төрт Grand Slam жарысының үшеуінде топ жарды. Яғни, ол биыл қаңтарда Australian Open жарысын, 2022 жылы Уимблдон турнирін жеңген. Енді Парижде грунтта өтетін "Роллан Гаррос" турнирін ұту қалды. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Елена Рыбакина – әлемнің бірінші ракеткасы. Қазақстандық теннисші бұл жетістікке қалай жетті? Reuters агенттігі Рыбакина финалдағы ойынын "ғажап" деп бағалады. "Ресейде туып, Қазақстан атынан жарысқа қатысатын теннисшінің ұстамдылығы Соболенконың US Open жарысында 20 жеңістен тұратын сериясын үзді. Беларусь теннисшісі Серена Уильямс және Крис Эверт сияқты US Open жарысын үш рет қатарынан жеңе алмады" деп жазды Reuters. Америкалық агенттік 27 жастағы Рыбакинаның турнир алдында жарақат алып қалғанын еске салады. Қазақстан теннисшісі US Open турнирі алдында Цинциннатидегі жарыста аяқ жарақатына байланысты жартылай финал ойынын аяқтай алмаған еді. Осыдан соң оның US Open жарысына қатысуына қауіп төнген. Бірақ ол он күннің ішінде жарақатын емдеп, түбінде турнирдің жеңімпазы атанды. "ТЕМІРДЕЙ МІНЕЗ" Британиялық Guardian басылымы "Қазақстан теннисшісі екі апта бойы темірдей мінез көрсетіп, ғажап финалда басты қарсыласы Соболенконы жеңді" дейді. Басылым Рыбакинаның бұрынғы жылдары US Open жарысында жақсы ойын көрсете алмағанын, "бірақ бұл жолы адам сенгісіз психологиялық тұрақтылықпен жеңіске жеткенін" атап өтті. "Рыбакина сіңірін жарақаттап алып, турнир алдында бір апта жаттықпады әрі турнирге қатыспай қала ма деген күдік болды. Бұған әлемнің бірінші ракетасы атана аламын ба деген қысымды қосыңыз. Ал US Open жарысының екінші аптасында бұған дейін Grand Slam жарысын және олимпиаданы жеңген теннисшілермен ойын күтіп тұрды. Ол бұл сынақтың бәрін артқа тастады" деп жазды Guardian басылымы. Елена Рыбакина US Open турнирінің кубогымен. 12 қыркүйек 2026 жыл. Associated Press агенттігі "Елена Рыбакина Нью-Йоркке келіп, Арина Соболенкоға тиесілі барлық атақты әкетіп барады. Алдымен әлемнің бірінші ракеткасы атағын, енді US Open титулын алды" дейді. AP агенттігі Рыбакина US Open жарысындағы жеңісі үшін 5,5 млн доллар ұтқанын, бұл Grand Slam тарихындағы ең үлкен ақшалай сыйлық екенін атап өткен. "Соболенко 2,8 млн доллар ақшалай сыйақы алады, бірақ бұған оның көңілі толмады, себебі ол Рыбакинадан жеңілген сәтте ракетасын сындырып, қатты ашуланды" деп жазды AP. Арина Соболенко жеңілістен соң ракеткасын сындырды. 12 қыркүйек 2026 жыл. Катардың Al-Jazeera телеарнасының сайты "Рыбакина ғажап ойын көрсетіп, Арина Соболенконы титулынан айырып, тақтан түсірді" деп жазды. Елена Рыбакина – US Open және Grand Slam жарыстарын жеңген алғашқы қазақстандық теннисші. Ол әлемдік рейтингіде бірінші орынға шыққан тұңғыш қазақстандық әрі бұл белесті бағындырған әлемдегі 30-теннисші болмақ. Рыбакина Grand Slam жарыстарынан бөлек былтыр жылдың үздік сегіз теннисшісі қатысатын WTA Finals турнирін жеңген еді. Бұл турнирдің финалында да ол Соболенкодан басым түскен. РЫБАКИНАНҢ БҰҒАН ДЕЙІНГІ ЖЕҢІСТЕРІ "Соққылары таза, дыбысы да бөлек". Рыбакинаның Australian Open жарысындағы жеңісі Рыбакина Штутгардтағы жарыста жеңіске жетіп, Porsche көлігін мінді Теннисші Елена Рыбакина Australian Open жарысының финалына шықты "Өзімді қазақ сезінемін". Рыбакина мен Путинцеваның жеңісі де, Қазақстанға ауысуы да сөз болды Рыбакина WTA Finals турнирінде жеңіске жетті. Жеңісі үшін $5,2 млн алады "Корттағы машина әлі талай титул жеңеді". https://www.azattyq.org/a/adil-soz-total.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Қазақстанда Total.kz сайты бірқатар операторлардан ашылмай қалды 13 қыркүйек 2026 жыл, 19:31 Қазақстанда Total.kz сайты бірқатар операторлардан ашылмай қалды Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Total.kz жаңалықтар сайты 12 қыркүйекте ашылмай қалды. Редакция мұны мемлекеттік орган өкілінің өтінішін орындаудан бас тартқандығымен байланыстырады. Бұл жөнінде “Әділ сөз” баспасөз қорғау ұйымы хабарлады. Қордың дерегінше, сайтта "Көкжайлауды Айға айналдырамыз ба?: Almaty SuperSki жобасы ҚР Қылмыстық кодексіне қайшы" ("Превратим Кок-Жайлау в Луну?": проект Almaty SuperSki противоречит УК РК") атты мақала 12 қыркүйекте жарияланған. Онда жобаның Көкжайлаудағы экожүйеге, ондағы сирек өсімдік пен жануар түрлеріне ықтимал әсері жөнінде мамандар пікірі келтірілген. Редакцияның хабарлауынша, мақала жарияланғаннан кейін Total.kz сайтына мемлекеттік орган өкілі хабарласып, мақаланы уақытша жасыруды өтінген. Редакция материалды өшіруден немесе оған шектеу қоюдан бас тартқан. Көп кешікпей сайт "Қазақтелеком", Altel, Tele2, Activ және Kcell арқылы ашылмай қалған. Бірақ Beeline желісі арқылы сайт ашық тұр. 13 қыркүйекте кешке Азаттық Қазақтелеком провайдері арқылы сайтты ашуға тырысқанмен ашылмады. Ал Beeline байланыс жүйесімен сайт ашылады, бірақ жоғарыда аталған мақала ашылмайды. "Әділ сөз" қоры оқиғаны "өте алаңдатарлық" жағдай деп атады. "Мемлекеттік органның редакцияға журналистік материалды жасыру туралы өтінішпен жүгінуінің өзі ашық құқықтық негіздемені талап етеді. Бұдан кейін бірнеше байланыс операторында сайттың ашылмай қалуы қоғамдық маңызды ақпаратты таратуға кедергі келтіру мүмкіндігі туралы одан да көп сұрақ туғызады" деп жазды қор өкілдері. "Әділ сөз" мәдениет және ақпарат министрлігін мемлекеттік орган өкілінің қандай негізде Total.kz редакциясына хабарласқандығын анықтауға, сонымен бірге сайтқа қандай да бір шектеу шарасы қолданылғаны-қолданылмағанын айқындауға шақырды. Қор өкілдері ақпарат құралының жұмысына кедергі келтіру және журналистік материалды шектеудің нақты заңды негізі болуы керек және редакция қызметкерлеріне қысым жасау құралы ретінде пайдаланылмауы керек екенін атап көрсеткен. Әзірге, Қазақстан мәдениет және ақпарат министрлігі оқиғаға реакция білдірген жоқ. https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1001765/%.body: افزایش قیمت دلار در سالهای اخیر بهانهای برای بالا رفتن قیمت کالا و خدمات بوده است. در دهههای دورتر گرانی بنزین عامل بالا رفتن هزینهها اعلام میشد پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو - افزایش قیمت بنزین میتواند ظرف مدت کوتاهی در رشد نرخ تورم نمایان شود. به گزارش فرارو ؛ بنزین 10 هزار تومانی قبل از هر چیزی باعث بالارفتن انتظارات تورمی میشود. قدم بعدی بالا رفتن هزینه حمل و نقل است و آنوقت نوبت به اقلامی میرسد که وابسته به قیمت حمل و نقل و بنزین هستند. در دهههای قبل که دلار حال و روز این مقطع را نداشت، افزایش قیمت کالا و خدمات به گرانی بنزین و اخبار قیمت بنزین گره زده میشد و حالا هم پیشبینی میشود افزایش قیمت بنزین پتانسیل بالا بردن سطح قیمتها را دارد. تاثیر افزایش قیمت بنزین در تحریک انتظارات تورمی تغییر قیمت بنزین در سالهای دور بهانهای برای بالابردن قیمتها در بازار بوده است. با گذشت زمان و جهشهای ارزی دهه 90 و اوایل دهه 1400 قیمت دلار جایگاه بنزین را به عنوان دماسنج اصلی سنجش تورم در عموم جامعه گرفت. با این حال اگر اهل بازار باشید میدانید افزایش قیمت بنزین هنوز هم محرک قدرتمندی در حافظه تاریخی جامعه برای تغییر پیشدستانه قیمتها به حساب میآید. فعالان بخش خدمات، تعمیرگاهها، انبارداران و توزیعکنندگان کالا با استناد به بنزین 10 هزار تومانی دریافتی خود را پیش از وقوع تغییر در سایر هزینهها بالا میبرند. تجربه دورههای گذشته در سالهای 1386، 1389 و 1398 گواهی میدهد که موج روانی برآمده از گرانی بنزین فارغ از میزان واقعی مصرف سوخت بنگاهها دستکم 4 تا 7 درصد تورم روانی به معاملات نقدی بازار تحمیل میکند. تاثیر افزایش قیمت بنزین در رشد کرایه ناوگان حملونقل خرد ناوگان حملونقل درونشهری مثل آژانسهای قدیمی، خودروهای فعال در تاکسیهای آنلاین و تاکسیهای خطی بیشترین تغییر را پس از این تصمیم حس میکنند. سهمیه بنزین انواع وسایل نقلیه برای سواریهای شخصی ماهانه 60 لیتر نرخ اول و 50 لیتر نرخ دوم تعیین شده است. یک راننده در اسنپ و تپسی روزانه بین 20 تا 30 لیتر سوخت مصرف میکند. سهمیه تخصیصی 110 لیتری این رانندگان در 4 تا 5 روز ابتدایی هر ماه تمام میشود و فعلا مابقی پیمایش ماهانه از محل بنزین 10 هزار تومانی تامین خواهد شد. پیش خودتان هزینه سوخت یک راننده تاکسی اینترنتی با کارکرد روزانه 200 کیلومتر را در نظر بگیرید. پیش از این با بنزین سه هزار یا پنج هزار تومان این هزینه تامین میشد و حالا با جهش به نرخ 10 هزار تومان، ماهانه بیش از چیزی نزدیک چهار میلیون تومان هزینه بیشتر برای او تراشیده میشود. کارشناسان اعتقاد دارند افزایش قیمت بنزین میتواند آرامآرام در بالا رفتن نرخ تورم تاثیر داشته باشد تاثیر افزایش قیمت بنزین در سرایت به بهای تمامشده کالاها انتقال کالا در هر بخشی از میادین مرکزی میوه و ترهبار تا بنکداریها و سردخانهها به مغازههای سطح شهر بر دوش ناوگان سبک حمل بار مثل وانتبارها، نیسانها و پیکهای موتوری قرار دارد. رانندگان این وسایل نقلیه پس از پایان سهمیه ماهانه، ناچار به تهیه سوخت با بهای لیتری 10 هزار تومان هستند. همین موضوع میتواند کرایه حمل هر بار وانت از میدان مرکزی ترهبار تهران به گوشه و کنار شهر را بالا ببرد یعنی به شکل غیرمستقیم ممکن است به قیمت کالاهای موجود در مغازهها اضافه شود. شاید به خاطر افزایش قیمت بنزین آزاد حجم مراجعه به سامانه سوخت من بالا رفته باشد اما به هر حال در یک برههای از ماه سهمیه بنزین یارانهای برای این بخش از راننددهها تمام میشود و چارهای جز استفاده از بنزین آزاد نمیماند. یعنی افزایش قیمت بنزین به فاکتورهای فروش در میادین میوه و مراکز توزیع خرد سرایت میکند. سیستمهای پخش قطعات یدکی و لوازم خانگی نیز ممکن است کرایه ارسال بار را در فاکتورهای جدید بالا ببرند. اثر کاهشی در بودجه خانوار افزایش همزمان کرایههای حملونقل و رشد قیمت اقلام مصرفی در بازار سهم هزینههای گریزناپذیر را در سبد خرج خانوادهها بالا میبرد. وقتی اعضای خانواده برای رفتوآمد روزانه خود هزینه بیشتری میپردازند و همزمان بابت خرید میوه، سبزیجات و مواد غذایی فاکتورهای گرانتری تسویه میکنند، سهم بزرگی از درآمد ماهانه آنها بلعیده میشود. این رشد اجباری در هزینههای پایه سبب میشود پول باقیمانده در دخل ماهانه خانواده برای مدیریت سایر بخشها محدود شود. افزایش قیمت بنزین با تحمیل هزینههای زنجیرهای توان مالی را برای سایر خریدها تقلیل میدهد. با پرداخت ارقام بیشتر برای ایابوذهاب و تامین خوراک منابع مالی در دسترس برای اموری مثل سلامت و درمان، آموزش، تفریح، خرید لباس یا تعویض لوازم خانگی از دسترس خارج میشود. هدایت بخش اضافهای از درآمد به سمت هزینههای حملونقل و مایحتاج روزمره خانوادهها را ناچار به خط زدن برنامههای رفاهی و انقباض بودجه سایر بخشها میکند. تبلیغات تاریخ واریز حقوق شهریور بازنشستگان تامین اجتماعی یارانه شهریور کی واریز میشود؟ تاثیر بنزین ۱۰ هزار تومانی در کف بازار طرح فروش سایپا؛ کوییک بخریم یا آریا اتوماتیک؟ بیشتر بدانید: نرخ تورم قیمت بنزین افزایش قیمت بنزین تبلیغات سوخت من؛ راهنمای کاربردی دریافت کارت سوخت نمایش دستی قیمت بنزین در جایگاههای سوخت! قیمت بنزین عوض شد؛ همهچیز درباره نرخ سوم در جایگاهها

https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1001854/%.body: عبدالواحد ابو راس از آمادگی یمن برای «صلح عادلانه» و پایان بخشیدن به محاصرات علیه صنعا خبر داد. پ ، پـ فرارو- عبدالواحد ابو راس، معاون وزیر امور خارجه یمن، در دیدار امروز خود از طریق ویدئو کنفرانس با هانس گروندبرگ، فرستاده ویژه دبیرکل سازمان ملل متحد به یمن، بر آمادگی صنعا برای دستیابی به صلح عادلانه و پایان دادن به حملات و محاصره علیه یمن مجدداً تأکید کرد. به گزارش فرارو به نقل از خبرگزاری رسمی یمن SABA، ابو راس اظهار داشت: رسیدگی به وضعیت انسانی کلید حل سایر مسائل است وعدم پاسخگویی سعودی به درخواستهای صنعا در این زمینه، منجر به وضعیت فعلی شده است که مسئولیت آن بر عهده سعودی است. وی همچنین در مورد عملیات انجام شده توسط نیروهای مسلح در برخی از مناطق ساحل غربی بحث کرد و تأیید کرد که وضعیت پایدار است و دولت یمن به وظیفه خود برای رسیدگی به وضعیت انسانی در آن مناطق عمل میکند. وی همچنین تأکید کرد که ناوبری دریایی امن است و محاصره فقط شامل کشتیرانی عربستان سعودی میشود و قبل از وقایع اخیر اعمال شده است و حمایت صنعا را از تلاشهای فرستاده ویژه برای دستیابی به صلح در یمن ابراز کرد. از سوی دیگر، فرستاده ویژه سازمان ملل متحد بر تعهد سازمان ملل متحد برای انجام تلاشها برای کاهش درگیری و دستیابی به صلح در یمن تأکید کرد. اعلام آمادگی انصارالله به سازمان ملل برای «صلح عادلانه» اسلامآباد به تلاشهای خود برای صلح در منطقه ادامه میدهد ترامپ: جنگ ایران پس از انتخابات تمام میشود چرا برخی فلسطینیها پرچم آمریکا را نصب میکنند؟ بیشتر بدانید: عربستان یمن صلح سفر فرمانده سنتکام به عربستان در بحبوحه تحولات یمن خسارات حملات حوثیها به جنوب عربستان جزئیات حمله پهپادی عربستان به شمال یمن

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/23.body: Listen (7 mins) Save Share Kazakhstan parliamentary elections begin: What’s at stake? on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google A woman casts her ballot at a polling station during early parliamentary elections in Almaty, Kazakhstan [Vladimir Tretyakov/AP Photo] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 23 Aug 2026 23 Aug 2026 | Updated: 23 Aug 2026 10:35 AM (GMT) Updated: 23 Aug 2026 10:35 AM (GMT) Voting is under way in Kazakhstan for a snap parliamentary election that is expected to strengthen President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s rule over the country. The last parliamentary elections were in 2023. The election comes just weeks after Kazakhstan, a nation of 21 million that borders Russia and China, revamped its legislative system by introducing constitutional changes and shifting from a dual-chamber parliament to a single-chamber one as it seeks to assert itself as a major democratic power in Central Asia. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Kazakhstan’s train hospital brings healthcare to remote regions list 2 of 3 Germany arrests Kazakhstan citizen accused of spying for Russia list 3 of 3 Kazakhstan releases first tiger to restore extinct species end of list How does the election process work and what’s at stake? Here’s what we know: When is the election happening? Elections for the 145 seats of the Kurultai, the country’s new unicameral legislature, is taking place on Sunday. To enter government, parties must receive at least 5 percent of the overall vote. Before July 1, when Kazakhstan’s new constitutional system came into effect, the parliament was bicameral, with the Mazhilis (lower house) and Senate (upper house). On the day the new system came into effect, President Tokayev signed a decree calling the snap election. According to national media outlet Astana Times, under the previous system, “legislation passed through the Mazhilis before moving to the Senate. Under the new model, the Kurultai concentrates legislative consideration, and adopted laws are then sent to the President.” Under the new constitutional system, presidents will only be permitted to serve a single, seven-year term. However, when his current, second term as president is up, Tokayev will be able to run for a third seven-year term of office, since the introduction of the new legislature resets his time in office. Advertisement He won the last presidential election, in 2022, with more than 80 percent of the vote, having run largely unchallenged, as all five of his competitors were unknowns. International observers will attend the parliamentary election on Sunday. The OSCE Parliamentary Assembly announced last week that nearly 80 parliamentarians and staff from about 30 countries would be deployed to observe the election. Pedestrians walk past an electronic screen promoting the Adilet (Justice) party before Kazakhstan’s upcoming parliamentary election in Almaty, Kazakhstan, August 17, 2026 [Pavel Mikheyev/Reuters] Who is contesting in this year’s election? Seven political parties are fielding candidates in this year’s elections. These include the newly formed Adilet party, Auyl, Aq Jol, the People’s Party of Kazakhstan, the Nationwide Social Democratic Party, Baytaq, and Respublica. Amanat, the party that has dominated Kazakh politics under various names since the 1990s, officially voted to dissolve itself into Adilet – which means “Justice” – a new party led by top aides to Tokayev, in June this year, largely to distance itself from Amanat’s former leader, the previous President Nursultan Nazarbayev. Nazarbayev , who was once close to Tokayev and considered his mentor, was the country’s president from 1991 to 2019. While he led economic modernisation of the country, his rule was defined by corruption, civil unrest and authoritarianism. He was elected president five times in widely criticised votes. In the run-up to the election on Sunday, Adilet has been running on the campaign message of “Just Kazakhstan”, pledging to raise household incomes, strengthen the country’s economy and improve public services, infrastructure and digitalisation. Around Almaty, Kazakhstan’s largest city, election posters – mostly in support of Adilet – have been ubiquitous for weeks, the Reuters news agency reported. Opinion polls suggest the new party is likely to win a large majority of the vote, with a number of smaller opposition parties, which analysts also consider broadly loyal to Tokayev, also likely to enter parliament. The Aq Jol Democratic Party is running on a campaign pledging support for entrepreneurship, while the Auyl party is advocating for stronger rural communities and the Baytaq Green Party is campaigning on the environment. Kazakh political analyst Rustam Burnashev told Reuters that while this snap election offers Tokayev a chance to remove figures associated with his predecessor, Nazarbayev, from the political stage, major reform of the political system is unlikely. Advertisement Despite the new Adilet party having been formed to distance itself from Nazarbayev’s legacy, analysts say little is likely to change materially. “All the parliamentary candidates are known,” Burnashev said. “Nor can one say that the parliament itself will be a transformative one.” Although Kazakhstan has enjoyed rapid economic growth in recent years, tax rises and inflation have hit living standards. Atapsha, a fruit seller who declined to give his full name, told Reuters that he would cast a vote, but without any particular expectations. “I am 73 years old. I’ve been waiting for things to get better for 73 years, but so far, nothing has really worked out. Still, I hope that this year things will finally improve.” What’s at stake? In 2022, Tokayev launched the “New Kazakhstan” package of reforms for the political system. A referendum was held on the legislative changes, which came in in July. Analysts say the upcoming elections will determine if the country’s new leaders can adhere to the renewed unicameral legislature and uphold its foreign policy. Besides these changes in the country’s legislative makeup, the elections come at a time when Astana is trying to showcase itself as a democracy and key power in Central Asia. To this end, Tokayev has focused on revamping the country’s infrastructure and economy and expanding ties with both China and the European Union. The country has also been beefing up relations with the United States in recent years. Last November, Kazakhstan signed a $4.2bn agreement with the US locomotive parts maker Wabtec. According to the US Department of Commerce, the deal will provide Kazakhstan with 300 kits to build locomotives for the Kazakh national rail company, Kazakhstan Temir Zholy. US President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to trumpet the deal, referring to it as “the largest Railroad Equipment Purchase in History”. Traditionally close to Russia, the country has preferred to play a neutral role in Moscow’s war on Ukraine and has called for peace. It has also offered itself as a venue for peace talks in the US-Iran war. In an article published in April by the Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs at Harvard Kennedy School, Nargis Kassenova wrote: “Kazakhstan has begun positioning itself as a middle power.” According to the Bureau of National Statistics, Kazakhstan’s gross domestic product (GDP) increased by 6.5 percent to about US$335bn in 2025 compared with last year, using the consumption method of calculations. “While a ‘lightweight’ by conventional standards, it has assets that make it significant for the rest of the world. Its geostrategic location at the heart of Eurasia makes it both an important connector and buffer between Europe, Russia, the Middle East, South Asia, and East Asia. It is also a regional leader in Central Asia,” she wrote. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/09/04/kak-per.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Издание Temirov Live выпустило расследование о том, кто стоит за первым автозаводом в Кыргызстане — в деле снова и снова всплывает Управделами президента, причем не только само ведомство, но и родная сестра главы госоргана Каныбека Туманбаева. Капсулу под строительство завода еще в 2024 году заложил президент Садыр Жапаров. В администрации президента сообщали , что завод стоимостью в 115 млн долларов будут строить «местные предприятия совместно с китайской компанией», но тогда в пресс-релизах ведомства не было никакой конкретики. Журналист Болот Темиров, ссылаясь на выписку из Госреестра прав на недвижимое имущество, сообщил, что земля под строительство автомобильного завода была государственной — право управлять участком земли до закладки капсулы получило Управление делами президента, которое возглавляет Каныбек Туманбаев. На следующий день после закладки капсулы была зарегистрирована компания « Китайско-Кыргызская совместная автомобильная производственная компания “Жису” » . Именно на эту компанию спустя четыре месяца после закладки капсулы было переписано право на пользование землей, где запланировано строительство завода. Управделами президента всплывает в истории не только через владение землей под завод. Ведомство — один из трех учредителей компании «Жису». Два других — это «Модуль Хаус» и «Хубэй Цзису Инвестиция». Компанией «Модуль Хаус» управляют два кыргызстанца. Уже знакомый нам по расследованиям друг Рустама Жапарова рэп-музыкант Эламан Токтобеков. Рустам Жапаров — сын президента Кыргызстана Садыра Жапарова. И Жыпаргуль Базарбаева, родная сестра Каныбека Туманбаева. А это нарушение Закона о конфликте интересов. Чиновникам запрещается заключать договоры с членами семьи, учитывая их личную заинтересованность. Но Управделами, которым руководит Туманбаев, допустил до строительства завода компанию его родной сестры. Еще чиновникам такого ранга запрещается иметь иностранное гражданство, но у Туманбаева как и у его сестры имеется действующее российское гражданство. «Раньше мы показывали, как господряды получают люди из президентского окружения. Здесь схема другая. Госучреждение само становится совладельцем компании вместе с ними [людьми из окружения]», — объясняет Темиров. А что касается инвестора? Публично это Hubei Zhuoyue, но в выписке минюста упоминается «Хубэй Цзису Инвестиция». Болоту Темирову не удалось обнаружить в реестре китайских компаний компанию с таким названием. «На каких условиях «Жису» получила право пользоваться госземлей? Был ли конкурс при выборе частного партнера? Почему именно «Модуль Хаус»? И кто такие «Хубэй Цзису Инвестиция»?» — задает вопросы Болот Темиров. ЭТО МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ ИНТЕРЕСНО ЕЩЕ ОТ АВТОРА Коргонбай Молл. Друг Ташиевых строит в Ноокате рынок, который не нравится ни акиму, ни торговцам Обход санкций через Африку. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/09/10/ne-budu.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Политик Темирлан Султанбеков написал письмо с обращением к президенту Садыру Жапарову из СИЗО-1. Он не стал просить милости и снисхождения. Он просит открытого суда: «Не считайте упорством и высокомерием, если я не следую обычаю других политиков умолять Вас о пощаде и стараться растрогать Ваше сердце. У меня есть, как и у других, родственники, близкие и друзья, которые могли бы предстать перед Вами в слезах и стараться вызвать жалость общества. Знаю Вашу любовь к таким сценам, но опозорить кыргызский дух и опуститься до столь недостойного поведения я не могу. Я всегда говорил о том, что нельзя жертвовать честью ради жизни или даже свободы». «У меня на днях день рождения, и я впервые хотел бы попросить у Вас кое-что. Конечно, о справедливом суде я просить не смею, так как это все равно что просить парикмахера сделать операцию на сердце. Я лишь прошу об открытом суде над нами. Если Вы уверены в справедливости и грамотности следствия, милиции, прокуроров и судей, то зачем бояться открытого суда? Дайте мне хоть 20 лет, хоть пожизненное, я к этому равнодушен, но проведите открытый суд, разве я этого не заслуживаю?» Также в письме Султанбеков рассказал, с каким давлением столкнулось его окружение — от коллег до семьи и даже кота: «Гонениям и арестам подверглась моя команда: в тюрьмах сидели и сидят мои заместители, руководители моего аппарата, советники, секретари и даже водитель, уголовное дело возбуждено также против моего помощника-ассистента». «Давление на меня на этом не завершилось и коснулось моей семьи. Все мои родственники покинули госслужбу. Недавно руководитель отдела информационной политики Вашей администрации Д. Орунбеков опубликовал «расстрельный список», куда включили мою маму и мою сестренку». «Сотрудники милиции силой отобрали телефон и планшет даже у моего 12-летнего братишки и не возвращают вот уже 10 месяцев. Ситуация доходит до смешного: милиционеры пинали и хватали моего кота, отобрали паспорт и ветеринарную книжку, и не отдавали полгода, решая, что делать с документами домашнего питомца — и это работа следствия?» Дело против Султанбекова и Атамбаева младшего Кадырбек Атамбаев и Темирлан Султанбеков, и ряд других лиц, связанных с бывшим президентом Алмазбеком Атамбаевым, были задержаны 22 ноября 2025 года, накануне выборов в парламент. После задержания спецслужбы распространили видео, на котором Темирлан Султанбеков сидя на кухне рассуждал с неизвестным мужчиной о политике. Неизвестный задавал наводящие вопросы о президенте и главе ГКНБ. Султанбеков в видео заявил, что экс-премьер Сапар Исаков мог бы быть президентом, и что через пару лет, а то и раньше в Кыргызстане сменится власть. В МВД утверждают, что массовые задержания, обыски и допросы проводились, чтобы пресечь деятельность «деструктивной группы», которая якобы готовила массовые беспорядки после выборов в Жогорку Кенеш. Кадыр Атамбаев считает, что по факту — он заложник для власти и инструмент давления на его отца Алмазбека Атамбаева, бывшего президента Кыргызстана.
